correctness.rationale: Distributional derivative represents each BV input as a signed superposition of jumps plus a constant. The exactly integrated single-step hat profile gives C1 and Cinf, and direct derivatives on the three admissible nodal branches prove the two thresholds. Each sharp constant is attained by a step. Node-difference averaging proves TV diminution. Standalone stdlib rational tests verify 36,534 step phases and 2,500 signed multi-jump inputs; tests are corroborative, not a substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: A natural affine-reproducing TVD reconstruction admits two independent sharp jump-error criteria. Full bandwidth classification reveals a concrete nontrivial design tradeoff: increasing averaging width to \(3\(h/2\)\) decreases worst uniform jump error to \(49/96\) without increasing the sharp integrated jump loss \(h/2\), while wider boxes worsen integrated loss. Exact phase transitions at \(2h/3\) and \(3\(h/2\)\) expose the migration of extremizing jumps and offer a usable quantitative shock-resolution design benchmark.
